headline: Impairment charge sinks profit; adjusted earnings edge up
summary_short: Dominion Energy reported GAAP EPS of $0.37 (vs $0.88 a year ago) as a $626M nonregulated asset-impairment charge weighed on results, while non-GAAP operating EPS rose to $0.79 from $0.75 and the company reaffirmed FY2026 operating EPS guidance of $3.45-$3.69.
summary_long: Revenue rose 17.6% y/y to $4,480M, but GAAP net income fell to $340M ($0.37/share) from $760M ($0.88/share) as the company recognized $626M of nonregulated asset impairments — mainly an $820M renewable-natural-gas charge and $78M solar charge, partly offset by a $195M Millstone asset-retirement-obligation benefit — plus $13M of NextEra merger-related costs. Non-GAAP operating earnings, which exclude these items, rose to $712M ($0.79/share) from $649M ($0.75/share), led by a $121M gain in the Dominion Energy Virginia segment from 2025 biennial-review impacts and rider equity returns. Dominion reaffirmed full-year 2026 operating EPS guidance of $3.45-$3.69 (midpoint $3.57) and all other 2026 guidance from its Q4 2025 call.
